updates.reason: Historical SGD-regime context, superseded by H7 (Muon) and H2 (schedule). Its only evidence token (E009-) does not match its 'supported' status (review). It is kept as a record of the SGD lessons (E008, E009, E015, E005, E017) and is no longer a decision driver.

Status stays refuted, but the evidence tokens are wrongly signed: E020 and E024 refute H5 (they are not E020+/E024+). E027, E030, E031, E033 and E034 test Muon hyperparameters (H7.1/H7.2), not whether Muon helps, and should be read under H7.x. Substantive refutation: E019 (+1.14 pp) and E044 (head on Muon, +0.32 pp).

updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work and per-step overhead drive the score. The tip is E046: bs 1536, 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs, compiled Muon on 9 convs plus the head, 4.955 s, two-run mean 0.7548. Cost table at bs 1536 (E045): 16 px 0.265 s (0.30x), 24 px ~0.52 s (0.59x), 32 px ~0.885 s/epoch (1.0x). The 32 px tail is ~71% of the time. 24 px is the minimum useful bridge (E032, E041). Only the 16 px phase is overhead-bound; 24 and 32 px sit at the 400 W cap (E045). Width cuts (E017, E050) and larger low-res batches (E043) trade badly. The remaining time levers, ranked by accuracy risk: (a) zero-accuracy compile configuration (static per-resolution graphs, measured -1.6% untimed; global max pool); (b) one fractional schedule trim (~0.03 pp per 1%, noisy); (c) per-step levers in the 16 px phase only (ceiling ~3%, transfer poorly to the 300 W PCIe judge).
updates.reason: The old text was stale: it named 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 as the schedule and said every schedule kept 8 epochs and one batch size, which E043, E046 and E047 contradict. Rewritten around the E046 tip and the E045 cost table. The static-shape result from E045's follow-up is now owned by new Lvl2 N1.

updates.statement: Phase-dependent bottleneck (E045, nvidia-smi at 100 ms on the tip). In the 32 px phase the GPU is at the 400 W cap 94-100% of the time, so time tracks fwd/bwd energy and hidden CPU gaps cost nothing (also E004, E010, E011). The 24 px phase is at the cap 84% of the time (391 W mean), so it is mostly energy-bound too. Only the 16 px phase (282 W mean, never at the cap, util 82%, ~16% of the time) is overhead- or launch-bound, and that is where bs 1024->1536 saved ~2 ms per removed step (E038). Per-step levers (CUDA graphs, NS overlap, fewer launches) can therefore gain at most ~0.14 s (~3%), and only in the 16 px phase. They transfer worse to the 300 W PCIe judge than FLOP-neutral compile fixes or FLOP-reducing levers. Prefer those on local ties.
updates.reason: E045 confirms the 32 px energy-bound and 16 px overhead-bound halves. It refutes the claim that 24 px is per-step-bound. Statement narrowed to what was measured.

This is a conjunctive prediction. The 32 px part held (cap 94-100%) and the 16 px part held (never at the cap). The 24 px part failed: the phase was at the cap 84% of the time, versus the predicted <90% of the cap for >=30% of the time. The verdict is therefore split and the prediction as written is refuted. The surviving content has moved into H2.4.

updates.statement: Untimed CUDA-event and profiler timing of the E046 tip per phase. Per step, wall time exceeds GPU-busy time by >=30% at 16 px, and by <10% at both 24 px and 32 px (E045: 24 px is at the cap 84% of the time). Observational only. This gates H2.12.1 and N2c.
updates.reason: Rescoped to the E046 tip. Per E045 the 24 px phase is expected to be cap-bound, not overhead-bound, so the 24 px expectation is reversed.

updates.statement: Only the 16 px phase is launch- or per-step-bound (E045: 282 W, util 82%, ~0.8 s of the tip's time). Capturing the whole train step (fwd, bwd, SGD foreach, compiled Muon, lookahead) in a CUDA graph for the 16 px shape alone removes idle gaps there. The ceiling is ~0.14 s (~3%), with a realistic gain of 1-2%. Graphing 24/32 px gains nothing because those phases sit at the power cap. Fable shows per-resolution whole-step graphs are feasible but publishes no isolated gain, and its 7.6% came mostly from resizing. The gain is per-step, so it transfers poorly to the 300 W PCIe judge.
updates.reason: E045 refutes the idea that the 24 px phase is launch-bound, and search found no isolated graph gain in Fable. Rescoped to 16 px only, with the ceiling lowered.

updates.statement: On the E046 tip (after static shapes, N1a, if that is banked), CUDA-graph the full train step for the 16 px shape only. Capture and warm it up in build on synthetic data, with static input buffers, the LR as 0-d tensors, and a renorm on/off graph-key variant. Prediction: time drops by >=1% (<=4.905 s on E046, or 1% below the N1a tip) with a two-run accuracy >=0.7535. Gate: run only if H2.4.2 shows wall time >=1.3x GPU-busy time at 16 px.
updates.reason: Rescoped to 16 px with a 1% bar: at util 82% over ~0.8 s, the ceiling is ~3%.

E043 effectively ran H2.11.1 (bs 2048 for the low-res phases, bs 1024 for the tail on a bs-1024 base). It cost -0.49 pp for -1.1% time, against the premise that large batches only hurt in the tail. One confound remains: sample-indexed schedules halved the warmup steps, and E051 shows fewer warmup steps cost ~0.2 pp. hiverge and Fable both keep bs 1536 fixed. Not closed on one confounded run, but the prior is low.
E043 is this experiment: 0.7493, below the predicted >=0.755. Time was 5.159 s, so the time part held.

updates.statement: On the E046 tip (bs 1536), raise only the 16/24 px phases to bs 3072, except the first 0.5 epoch, which stays at bs 1536. The 32 px tail stays at bs 1536. Keep the LR warmup fixed in steps (not samples), so the E043 warmup confound is removed. Decay, EMA and lookahead are indexed by samples. Prediction: time <=4.85 s (>=2% below E046) with a two-run accuracy >=0.7535. Low priority: run only after H8.1.1 indicates whether early batch size, not warmup steps, drove E043's loss.
updates.reason: Rebased onto E046 and the warmup confound removed, per the review. The prior is lowered by E043.

updates.statement: Zero-time-cost accuracy levers can buy 0.15-0.3 pp of slack to spend on schedule trims. Under SGD they gave nothing (E008, E009, E015). Under Muon, LS (E037), head LR (E049) and halved warmup (E051, -0.2 pp) gave nothing, and every one of these is a single run within noise. Untested candidates whose optimum plausibly moved at ~256 steps (bs 1536): a longer warmup (H6.4), a lower Muon LR floor or a short final EMA (H6.5, as in Fable: 0.05 floor, EMA over the last ~8 steps), and a Muon-lr re-check at bs 1536 (H7.1).
updates.reason: Updated with E049 and E051, and with Fable's floor/EMA settings found by search. Not closed: every Muon-era null is a single within-noise run.

updates.statement: bs 1536 cut the run to ~256 steps, but the LR warmup was only rescaled from a schedule tuned at ~408 SGD steps. Halving the warmup cost ~0.2 pp (E051, a single run within noise). Its sign, together with E043's warmup-step confound, points toward early training being step-starved, so a longer warmup may help (see H8). Doubling is untested, and so is the post-mortem mechanism that the warmup protects the 64x-LR SGD BN-bias and whitening-bias groups.
updates.reason: Reopened per the review. One run in one direction does not close warmup, and H6.4.1 itself called for testing both directions.
E051: halving the warmup gave 0.7528, -0.2 pp vs 0.7548, not the predicted >= +0.2 pp. The 'both within ±0.15 pp, so closed' clause did not trigger, because doubling was never run (now N3a).

Search: the tuned Fable Muon-style recipe uses a 0.05 floor with a 0.375-epoch constant tail and an EMA over only the last ~8 steps. This is plausible support for the direction, but not from CIFAR-100.

updates.statement: On the E046 tip, change the Muon-group LR floor from 0.07x to 0.05x and leave everything else unchanged. Prediction: 3-seed accuracy >=0.7563 (>= +0.15 pp over the 0.7548 two-run mean) at equal time (±0.5%). A tip requires a confirming rerun (H4 rule). A result within ±0.15 pp closes it.
updates.reason: Rebased onto the E046 tip and its two-run mean.

updates.statement: Accuracy and timing noise set the usable margin. There are four identical-rerun pairs on compiled-Muon tips: E026/E028 differed by 0.22 pp, E038/E039 by one test image, E044/E045 were bit-identical, and E046/E048 differed by 0.10 pp (E048's 4.971 s indicates E046 code ran despite its 'E044' label; verify the commit). The nondeterminism is bimodal: either a full trajectory divergence (cuDNN algorithm picks, E036/E042) or none, or an eval-only difference. Bit-identical pairs carry no information about variance, so the 3-seed run-to-run sd (~0.1-0.15 pp) rests on two divergent pairs. Per-seed sd over seeds 3-10 is 0.22-0.38 pp. Tip E046: two-run mean 0.7548, seeds 3-10 0.7542, 11-seed ~0.7544. That leaves ~0.15 pp of margin on the local 0.753 gate and ~0.45 pp on the official 75%. Rule for a new tip: a 3-seed mean >=0.755, or two non-bit-identical runs averaging >=0.7535. Time noise is ~0.3%.
updates.reason: The noise model was stale (n=2). Updated with all four pairs, the bimodality, the E048 margin check and the mislabel note from the review.
E048 (E046 code): seeds 3-10 mean 0.7542, within 0.15 pp of the 0.7548 seeds 0-2 two-run mean and >=0.7530. Note the prediction was written for E038 but was tested on E046.

updates.statement: The tip's run-to-run nondeterminism comes from per-process cuDNN algorithm picks (cudnn.benchmark), not from Muon max-autotune. E036 (deterministic cuDNN plus default-mode Muon) gave a bit-identical seed-0 rerun. E042 (default-mode Muon only) stayed nondeterministic (0.7522/0.7549/0.7530). Pinning cuDNN costs ~9.8% time (E036), so determinism is not usable in scored runs. It is a measurement convenience, not a score lever. AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1)'s atomic backward is an unlikely co-source: with a 1x1 output, each gradient goes to a single argmax and nothing collides.
updates.reason: E036 and E042 together isolate cuDNN picks. Muon autotune as the source is refuted, and the restoration-at-no-cost part is refuted on time.
E036 was bit-identical but cost +9.8% time (6.008 s vs the <=+1.5% predicted). E042 shows default-mode Muon alone does not give determinism.
E042 is this probe. Seed-0 reruns were not bit-identical (0.7522/0.7549/0.7530), which by the hypothesis's own conditional attributes the nondeterminism to cuDNN benchmark picks.

updates.statement: 16 px epochs are cheap (0.30x of a 32 px epoch at bs 1536, E045), and replacing an early 24 px epoch costs roughly 0.2-0.35 pp per swap: ~0.2 pp each for the first two, ~0.2-0.3 pp for the third (E029, E040, E046), and ~0.34 pp each for the 3rd+4th (E032, which removed the bridge). The 20 px bridge (E041, -0.38 pp for -4.5%) traded no better. E046 spent E044's +0.32 pp head-on-Muon margin on the third swap. With ~0.15 pp of margin left, no further whole-epoch swap is affordable; only fractional trims (H2.10) fit.
updates.reason: E046+ supports the per-swap cost. The old 'no further swap affordable' claim was overtaken by E046, which used new margin. E041 is better read as inconclusive or weakly negative than as clean evidence.

E045 measured a 12 px epoch at 0.186 s = 0.21x, just below the predicted >=0.22x floor, so the cost part is marginally refuted. The '<1.5% saving per swap, not worth pursuing' conclusion holds, and 12 px also needs static shapes (dynamic graphs crash). The 12 px line is retired.

updates.statement: Fractional, step-indexed schedule trims are the finest-grained schedule lever. E047 (2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 on E044) gave -0.16 pp for -5.2% (~0.03 pp per 1%). That is better than whole swaps or width cuts, but it was measured against a single trajectory (E045 was a bit-identical replay), so the uncertainty is about ±0.07 pp per 1%. A 32->24 whole-epoch swap cost ~0.5 pp (E025). Fractional trims of the 32 px tail (71% of the time) are untested. With ~0.15 pp of margin, at most one trim fits, and only under the two-run rule.
updates.reason: E047 supports it weakly; the review flags the single-trajectory reference. The stale 4@16 prediction is retired.
Stale. The predicted 5.45 s is slower than the 4.955 s tip, and E032 showed 4@16 costs 0.68 pp.
Concerns E006-era augmentation RNG and can no longer change any decision. Seed separation is evident from the per-seed spread on the tips.

updates.statement: Muon flattened the epoch slope, so a group-2 width cut might trade better than under SGD. E050 (384->352 on E046) saved only 2.6% time for -0.22 pp (~0.085 pp per 1%), worse than fractional trims (~0.03-0.04). The time saving was half the FLOP estimate. Candidate causes: 352 is not a multiple of 64 or 128, so tensor-core tiles pad it; and ~30% of the time is in low-res phases where group-2 FLOPs barely become time (16 px is overhead-bound). Not worth more scored runs unless a per-layer profile shows a tile-aligned width (320) with a much better time yield.
updates.reason: E050: the time prediction failed clearly (-2.6% vs >=3.5%, well outside the 0.3% time noise), and the accuracy was at the bar. One run, so the mechanism stays inconclusive and the prior drops.
E050: time -2.6% (predicted >=3.5%) and accuracy -0.22 pp (predicted <=0.2 pp). The exchange rate was 0.085 pp per 1%, not <=0.06.

updates.statement: Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~8 epochs (E008), and Muon was the lever. On the 9 group 3x3 convs it gave +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (0.54 vs 0.95 pp/epoch, E020) and good large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Putting the 576->100 head on Muon added ~+0.32 pp (E044); its size is uncertain (perhaps 0.15-0.35 pp) because it was never independently replicated (E045 was a bit-identical replay), and its mechanism is unknown (N4). Muon momentum, lr and LS were swept only on the bs-1024 E026 base with the head on SGD; NS count is closed (E031, E033). Each null is a single run near the noise floor, so 'closed' applies to that base, not to the bs-1536/head-Muon tip. Muon's per-step cost is cut mainly by fewer steps.
updates.reason: Added E044's head gain and its uncertainty (review). The 'closed' scope is limited to the base the sweeps ran on, because step-count transfer was not shown.

updates.statement: Muon momentum and lr were at a flat local optimum on the bs-1024, ~384-step E026 base with the head on SGD. Momentum is flat in 0.5-0.6 and steep above (0.85: -1.18 pp, E027, E030). LR is flat in 0.20-0.24 (E034). Whether this transfers to the bs-1536, ~256-step, head-on-Muon tip is untested. One Muon-lr point on E046 is the cheapest re-check (N5a), ranked below warmup doubling (N3a) and the Muon floor (H6.5.1).
updates.reason: Scoped to the base it was measured on (review: SGD-to-Muon non-transfer also applies across step counts).

updates.statement: Muon's remaining overhead is a fixed per-step cost (NS matmuls plus stacking/momentum kernels). bs 1536 saved ~2 ms per removed step, but only in the overhead-bound 16 px phase (E038, E045). Renorm cadence saved ~0.08 ms/step (E035). NS 3->2 cost 1.8 pp (E031) and NS 4 bought nothing (E033). At 24/32 px the GPU sits at the power cap, so further NS savings mostly trade FLOPs for energy. Turbo-Muon (AOL) saved only 0.8% on the CIFAR-10 speedrun when going from 5 to 4 iterations (search), so AOL + 2 iterations is expected to save <=1%. Drop-Muon (random layer subsets) is untested but has a low prior given E031.
updates.reason: Integrated E045's phase split and the search evidence on Turbo-Muon and Drop-Muon.

Search: Turbo-Muon measured only -0.8% on the CIFAR-10 airbench-style run when removing one of five iterations. Removing one of three is harsher (E031: -1.82 pp), and the expected saving is now <=1%, below the 1.5% estimate.

new.statement: Compile and graph configuration is a zero-accuracy, FLOP-neutral time lever, independent of the math. Automatic dynamic shapes (PyTorch's default after the 2nd input shape) produce slower generic kernels for the 24/32 px train graphs. Static per-resolution graphs saved ~0.086 s/trial (~1.6%) at equal math in E045's untimed micro-benchmark, and Fable's CIFAR-10 record sets automatic_dynamic_shapes=False. The global pool can also use flatten+amax instead of AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) (Fable: avoids slow atomic kernels). These levers should transfer to the PCIe judge, because they reduce kernel inefficiency rather than idle gaps.

On the E046 tip, set torch._dynamo.config.automatic_dynamic_shapes=False (and raise cache_size_limit) for the train graphs, so each (resolution, batch) train shape compiles statically and is warmed up in build. Eval stays dynamic, or is padded to warmed shapes, so any B from 1 to 1024 never recompiles at eval and finishes in under 5 s; verify untimed for B in {1, 7, 1000, 1024}. Change nothing else. Prediction: time <=4.89 s (>=1.3% below 4.955 s) and 3-seed accuracy >=0.7535 (unchanged within noise).

On the N1a tip (or E046 if N1a fails), replace AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).amax(dim=2), which is mathematically identical, and recompile and warm up in build. Prediction: time drops by >=0.5% with accuracy within noise (>=0.7535). A drop under 0.3% is time noise and means the pool is not a lever here.

On the E046 tip, overlap each layer's Muon momentum+NS update with the rest of backward (grad hooks firing per filter stack on a side CUDA stream, with an explicit sync before the next forward). Prediction: time drops by >=1% with bit-equivalent math (accuracy within noise, >=0.7535). Nearly all of the gain should come from the 16 px phase. Gate: H2.4.2 shows >=30% idle time at 16 px.

On the banked static-shape tip, compare two equal-time trims (~-0.26 s each): (A) 3@16 + 0.5@24 + 4@32 and (B) 3@16 + 1@24 + 3.7@32, with step-indexed switches and LR/EMA/lookahead/renorm rescaled to the step count. Prediction: A's two-run mean is >=0.7535, and B's 3-seed mean is >=0.1 pp lower than A's, because the 32 px tail is binding (E025). Only the variant that passes the H4 rule may become the tip.

Untimed per-layer CUDA-event profile at 32 px, bs 1536, on the E046 tip with group-2 widths 384, 352 and 320. Prediction: per channel removed, 352 recovers <=60% of its FLOP-proportional group-2 time at 32 px while 320 recovers >=80%, i.e. tile misalignment explains E050's shortfall. If 320 also recovers <80%, width cuts are dead and H2.13 is refuted.

On the E046 tip, double the LR warmup length for both the SGD and Muon groups, with the same peak and decay end point, and change nothing else. Prediction: 3-seed accuracy >=0.7563 (>= +0.15 pp over the 0.7548 two-run mean) at equal time (±0.5%). If the result is within ±0.15 pp, warmup length is closed in both directions.

Head-on-Muon's ~+0.32 pp (E044) comes mostly from a much larger effective step size on the 100-way head, not from orthogonalization itself. Under SGD the head (lr scaled by the kilostep rule, momentum, LS 0.3) moves slowly over ~256 steps. E049 (0.5x head LR, +0.1 pp, noise) cannot distinguish the two readings. If step size is the mechanism, cheaper head levers (wd, renorm, LR) could add margin.

On the E046 tip, move the head weight back to SGD, with its LR set so the per-step update RMS matches the Muon head's (measured untimed on the tip). Prediction: two-run accuracy >=0.7535 (within ~0.15 pp of 0.7548). If it lands at <=0.7520, orthogonalization rather than step size is the mechanism. Diagnostic run, not a time lever.

On the E046 tip (bs 1536, ~256 steps, head on Muon), change only the conv-filter Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.28 (0-d tensor, nothing recompiles). Prediction: 3-seed accuracy >=0.7563 (>= +0.15 pp over 0.7548) at equal time. A result within ±0.15 pp confirms that the bs-1024 lr optimum transfers.

The rerun nondeterminism is bimodal. Either training diverges (cuDNN algorithm picks, giving ~0.1-0.6 pp per-seed differences: E028, E048), or training is bit-identical and only eval or a very late step differs (E038/E039 differed by one test image). Only the training-divergence mode samples the variance that matters for decisions.

Untimed diagnostic: log a checksum of the final weights and BN buffers per seed at the end of train, for two fresh-process reruns of the E046 tip on seeds 0-2. Prediction: every seed whose test accuracy differs between reruns also has a different weight checksum (train divergence). No seed has identical weights but different accuracy; if one does, eval-shape cuDNN picks are a separate source and should be pinned in build.

Early-training fragility: in the ~256-step regime, the quantity and quality of the early updates bound final accuracy more than late-phase sample count does. Larger early batches (E043, -0.49 pp), shorter warmup (E051, -0.2 pp), 16 px replacing early 24 px epochs (E029, E032, E040, E046: ~0.2-0.35 pp each) and a 20 px bridge (E041) all cost accuracy, while a global bs 1536 cost little (E038) and tail-side levers behave smoothly. Levers that add early updates or stabilize early updates should buy margin cheaply; levers that coarsen early training should be avoided.

The early loss comes from too few effective updates, or from too high an LR on the SGD-trained BN biases and whitening bias (64x LR), before the features form. Mechanisms: fewer early steps (large batch, sample-indexed warmup) and noisier or lower-information early inputs (16 px) both hurt the same fragile early phase. hiverge and Fable train the whitening bias only for the first 20% of steps, which supports the bias-LR channel.

On the E046 tip, run the first 0.5 epoch (16 px) at bs 768 and the rest at bs 1536. The warmup is fixed in samples, so it gets more steps; SGD groups are scaled by the kilostep rule in the bs-768 phase and Muon lr/momentum are unchanged. The bs-768 16 px shape is warmed up in build. This adds ~16 steps, about +0.04 s. Prediction: 3-seed accuracy >=0.7563 (>= +0.15 pp over 0.7548) with time <=+1% of 4.955 s. A result within ±0.15 pp refutes the early-update-count channel.

On the E046 tip, halve the warmup only for the Muon groups and keep the SGD groups' warmup (BN biases, whitening bias, head bias) unchanged. Prediction: 3-seed accuracy >=0.7535 (no loss beyond noise vs 0.7548), unlike E051's -0.2 pp from halving both. That would show the warmup protects the SGD bias groups (the E051 post-mortem mechanism). If the result is <=0.7525, Muon itself needs the warmup.

structured_output.summary:
Tree revised around the E046 tip (4.955 s, two-run mean 0.7548, ~0.15 pp margin on the local 0.753 gate).

**Bookkeeping fixes:**
- H1 retired as SGD history.
- H5's misfiled tokens noted in the reason field (E020/E024 refute it; the Muon hyperparameter runs belong to H7.x).
- H2.4.1 refuted as a conjunction: 16 and 32 px held, but 24 px is power-capped.
- H2.11.1 refuted by E043; H2.11 lowered to inconclusive because of the warmup confound.
- H4.3.1 and H4.3.2 refuted (E036 cost +9.8%; E042 stayed nondeterministic). H4.3 rewritten: cuDNN algorithm picks are the source, and determinism is not a score lever.
- H6.4.1 refuted by E051, but H6.4 reopened, since one within-noise run in one direction does not close warmup.
- H2.13.1 refuted by E050; H2.13 is inconclusive pending a tile-alignment profile.
- H4.2.3 supported by E048.
- Retired: H2.10.1, H2.1.3 and H2.8.2.

**Rewritten statements:**

- H2.4: only the 16 px phase is overhead-bound.
- H2.12: 16 px only, 1–2% realistic.
- H4: four rerun pairs, bimodal nondeterminism, E048 mislabel.
- H7 and H7.1: Muon knobs are closed only on the bs-1024 base; the head gain is uncertain.
- H7.2 and H7.2.4: lowered using the Turbo-Muon search result.
